name: Demo_Day_Night_Cycle
description: Sub-feature of Environmental_Demo: Day/night lighting transition and its effect on education

questions.question: Can the player identify rock types from visual cues alone?
questions.answer: ZE47-1: Sun arc teaches time estimation (sun height = time). ZE47-2: Star sphere is world-aligned, enabling celestial navigation. ZE47-3: Temperature curve peaks 1-2h after solar noon (thermal inertia lesson). ZE47-4: Night changes observations (stars, condensation, cold-related geology). ZE47-5: 3 sub-features (Celestial_Light_Rotation, Temperature_Time_System, Night_Visibility_Gameplay) each drive specific education via shared time-of-day variable.

questions.question: Does the player learn to predict weather from cloud formations?
questions.answer: ZE47-2: Flat-bottom clouds = stable air (day). Towering clouds = storms building (afternoon). Star visibility = clear night. Cloud color at sunset predicts next-day weather. Each requires time-of-day-specific observation.

questions.question: Can curiosity-driven players discover deeper geology facts?
questions.answer: ZE47-3: Rocks cracked by thermal expansion at noon are visible cooling at night. Star patterns teach navigation — same constellation from different canyon locations. Deep geology: 'Why are some rocks cracked and others smooth?' leads to thermal expansion + mineral composition lesson.

questions.question: Does the environment teach something the player uses later in gameplay?
questions.answer: ZE47-4: At night: condensation observations near canyon walls (temperature drop + humidity). Day: mineral identification by color. Different rocks conduct heat differently — touch test. Noon observations (thermal expansion cracking) teach material properties used in shelter-building (Loop 6).
